title: How machines learn
objective: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to explain how a machine learns from labelled examples, make a guess by finding the closest example, and say why learning depends on good examples.

sections.title: Learning from labelled examples
sections.text: Many AI systems learn from labelled examples. A labelled example comes with the right answer, like a photo marked "cat" or a fruit marked "apple". The more good examples the machine sees, the better its guesses usually become.

sections.title: Guessing from the closest example
sections.text: One simple way to learn is to remember the examples and, for something new, find the example that is most similar. This is called a nearest neighbour guess. If a new fruit weighs about the same as the melons, the guess is melon.

sections.title: Learning from mistakes
sections.text: Many machines learn by making a guess, comparing it with the right answer, and changing a little to make a smaller mistake next time. They repeat this thousands or millions of times. Each change is small, but together they add up.

sections.title: Learning is not understanding
sections.text: A machine only learns what its examples show. If every cat photo it saw was of an orange cat, it may struggle with a black cat. It finds patterns in numbers. It does not understand the world the way you do.

examples.title: Example 1: A nearest neighbour guess
examples.code:
examples = [(120, "apple"), (150, "apple"), (300, "melon"), (350, "melon")]
new = 280
best = examples[0]
for e in examples:
    if abs(e[0] - new) < abs(best[0] - new):
        best = e
print(best[1])

examples.title: Example 2: Getting closer by fixing mistakes
examples.code:
guess = 0
target = 10
for step in range(5):
    mistake = target - guess
    guess = guess + mistake / 2
print(guess)

check_questions.prompt: A program learned to spot cats only from photos of orange cats. What is most likely?
options: It will spot every cat perfectly
It understands cats the way a person does
It will never make a mistake
It may struggle with cats of other colours
check_questions.explanation: A machine only learns what its examples show, so cats that look different may confuse it.

misconception.0: It only saw orange cats, so other cats may confuse it.
misconception.1: It finds patterns in numbers. It does not understand like a person.
misconception.2: Every AI system can make mistakes.
